newsitem.title: GERMANY: Bayer under small pressure on U.S. ruling.
newsitem.headline: Bayer under small pressure on U.S. ruling.

text.p: Shares in Bayer AG were slightly down in bourse trade on Thursday after a U.S. judge on Wednesday ordered the U.S. unit of the German chemicals group to pay a $50 million fine over price-fixing charges.
Bayer shares were down 96 pfennigs at 61.34 marks ($37.36) but off the low so far in bourse trading on Thursday at 61.21 marks.

"It's a small amount of money in the grand scheme of Bayer," said one Frankfurt trader about the fine to settle charges that Bayer was part of an international conspiracy to fix prices and allocate sales for citric acid.
"But it is more a burden on the sentiment about Bayer since there will be little, if any, financial impact from the ruling," the trader said.
Traders noted that other chemical industry shares, including Hoechst and BASF, were also lower on a general lack of interest in the sector despite the stronger dollar.
"One would think that chemical shares, with their reliance on the dollar, would be healthy," said the trader. "But there just does not seem to be much interest in the sector."
